deep.reconstruction:
This folio side (2v) carries no independent mathematical writing. The only real ink is the library stamp 'NIEDERSÄCHS. STAATS- U. UNIV. BIBLIOTHEK GÖTTINGEN'. The faint brownish script in the right column and centre is bleed-through (show-through) of the recto, folio 2r, which is the 'previous page' transcription. Three observations from the image show this:

(a) The writing is mirror-reversed. The line printed on 2r as 'Δλ'k = −ελ'(IV)' appears here with 'Δλk' at the far right edge and '=' to its left, i.e. in reversed order.

(b) The layout matches 2r line for line. The right column runs: 'Δλ'k = … −ελ' III', '+III ε.k', 'also Substitution −4III ε.k', '+λ'k bei ω', 'für (½−ω)M soll k=1', then a horizontal rule. Next come 'Δλ'k = −ελ'(IV)', '−(V)εk', '+4Vεk x ganz y gerade', 'also subtrahirt', '−ελ' = (V)+εk', '−(V) 4εk …', '−λ'k bei (½+ωi)M', '+λ'k bei (½+(½−ω)i)M'. The centre has the two small 2×2 boxes and the notes 'k = +1 für [X] gerade, [Y] ungerade, in allen andern Fällen = 0', 'Dieses für die Verwandlung der II', and 'k = +0 für [X] und [Y] zugl. gerade, +1 für alle andern Fälle'.

(c) The two dark ink blots match the dark spots that would be visible through the paper from the recto.

So there is nothing on this page to reconstruct beyond what belongs to 2r. For context only, 2r and 3r belong to Gauss's lattice-point work on biquadratic residues in the Gaussian integers, i.e. an analogue of the Gauss lemma / Eisenstein lattice-point proof for quartic reciprocity:
- On 2r he tracks how certain counts (λ', k) change (Δ) under substitutions. The parity indicators k are tabulated by the parity of [X], [Y], with the lattice points taken at positions (½+ωi)M etc.
- Folio 3r gives a worked example: m = 1+6i (norm 37), M = 5−4i (norm 41), μ = mM = 29+26i (norm 1517). It counts lattice points row by row (total 379) and tabulates the distribution of residues for m and M.
